strength: The 10:00 AM stays left of the same circle in all three views. Folder, tag and priority form one row, with the calendar and flag dates together below at both widths.
concern: The time almost touches the expanded card edge while the lower left quarter sits empty. The tiny calendar grid takes a closer look to distinguish from the flag.

strength: The open menu puts a check beside Planner and names Inbox explicitly. The bottom date arrows and far-right plus read as separate actions.
concern: Before opening the generic menu icon, Today is the only workspace cue. On arrival the center date control becomes a circle containing a dash, whose purpose is unclear.

strength: The stable circle column marks the start of each task, even with wrapping titles. Dimming the surrounding rows makes the expanded task easy to locate.
concern: The small pale project pills sit close to the next title. The expanded card leaves a wide empty gutter below the time and only a sliver of space between its left edge and 10:00 AM.

strength: Times, completion circles and flags keep their columns as titles wrap. The white expanded card keeps the 10 AM task identifiable against the dimmed list.
concern: Project pills are small and faint. The expanded time nearly touches the card edge while the two rows of controls leave a wide empty strip below it.

strength: The 10 AM label stays left of the circle in all three views. Project, tag and priority sit above the schedule and deadline, which fit side by side at both widths.
concern: The time has almost no left inset in the card. Aligning every property with the title leaves roughly a quarter of the narrower card empty below the time and circle, even as the date text is quite small.

strength: The open menu names all three workspaces and marks Planner with a check. The Inbox title confirms arrival, and the plus remains at the opposite end from the menu.
concern: Before opening the menu, Today and the three-line icon give little indication that Planner is the active workspace or that Inbox is available there. The lone dash in the center control on Inbox is unexplained.

strength: The menu names all three destinations and checks Planner. Its bottom-left position separates it from the centered date arrows and the capture plus.
concern: Before opening the menu, Today identifies the day but never names Planner. The three-line button gives little indication that it changes workspaces, and the lone dash in Inbox has no clear purpose.

strength: A consistent completion-circle column anchors each row, including wrapped titles. The selected task keeps its place as a white card against the dimmed list.
concern: The expanded time sits almost against the card edge while both property rows start at the title, leaving a wide blank area underneath the time. Small pale project tags are easy to skim past.

strength: 10:00 AM sits directly left of the circle at both widths. The calendar and flag controls fit side by side below the other properties and retain the same order.
concern: The time has almost no inset inside the card, yet the first quarter of each property row is empty. The fine outlines make the small tag and priority controls less prominent.

strength: The open menu labels all three destinations and places a check beside Planner. Inbox appears as the title on arrival.
concern: In the starting view, Today and a hamburger are the only clues to Planner navigation. The open menu also covers part of the date control.

strength: The menu sits directly beneath the title and keeps Inbox, the Planner check, and both bottom controls in view.
concern: Today with a downward chevron could just as readily open date choices. Planner is named only in the menu.

strength: The fixed circle and time columns keep wrapped titles aligned. A white card and dimmed list clearly isolate the expanded proof task.
concern: The Studio tag below the proof title nearly touches the next title. In the card the lower date pills sit close to the bottom edge.

strength: The 10 AM value stays on the left of the circle. Both widths keep project, tag and priority together above the paired dates.
concern: Aligning every property to the title leaves a wide empty area under the schedule and circle, even at 390 points.

strength: The persistent strip names Planner, Inbox and Projects. Its check and white selection move to Inbox while capture remains at bottom right.
concern: The destination strip costs a row of vertical space, and after arrival Inbox appears twice in close succession.

strength: At 440 points all five controls fit on one line. At 390 the two dates wrap together, with both rows starting at the same inset.
concern: Notes starts beneath the time column, creating a substantial leftward jump from the title directly above it.

strength: The bottom Planner label and chevron identify the switcher before it opens, and the same position reads Inbox on arrival.
concern: The expanded strip occupies the locations of both the date control and capture button, which disappear in the choices view.

strength: A divider separates the controls from Notes. Schedule and deadline lead the property strip at both widths and use the full left inset.
concern: At 390 points the project group wraps flush right, so the eye has to cross the card to find the beginning of its second row.

strength: The wrapped proof title, its Studio tag and the next title have distinct spacing. Notes and the two control rows also have visible separation inside the card.
concern: The trailing Tomorrow label sits near the wrapped proof title at 390 points, leaving a narrow gap between the two text columns.

strength: The gap after each project tag keeps it attached to its title, and the expanded card gives both rows of controls breathing room.
concern: The larger vertical gaps accumulate among the single-line rows. The 1 PM task already meets the bottom toolbar while several earlier tasks show only a title.

strength: The persistent labeled strip puts Inbox in sight before switching and moves the checkmark to it on arrival. The date arrows and plus occupy separate positions below.
concern: The strip costs a line of list height, and the lone minus below Inbox has no label.

strength: The time stays directly left of the circle through expansion. A divider introduces the controls, with the schedule and deadline together first and legible at both widths.
concern: At 390 pt the project, tag and priority move to the far right of the next line, so reading on from the dates requires a diagonal jump.

strength: On the wrapped proof task, the circle and flag flank a single title block, and Studio sits just below it. Expansion preserves the title position and leaves a clear gap before the next row.
concern: Pale, small project labels such as Studio take a closer look than the adjacent titles.

strength: The closed switcher names Planner and has a disclosure arrow. Opening it shows all three workspaces with a check at Planner, and the arrival control reads Inbox.
concern: Opening the chooser replaces the whole toolbar, so the date and capture controls lose their visible positions during selection.

strength: The menu directly beneath the title names each workspace, checks Planner and leaves the date arrows and capture button visible below.
concern: Before opening, Today and its small chevron suggest a date choice. The word Planner first appears inside the menu.

strength: The schedule remains aligned with the circle, and all properties fit in two consistently ordered groups at both widths.
concern: Even at 440 pt the controls start beneath the title, leaving the wide schedule gutter empty and putting the schedule chip on the second line.

strength: The condensed layout keeps the 1 PM task and two following titles fully visible. The expanded card clearly singles out the proof task.
concern: In the run from Approve the cover artwork to Review accessibility findings, each small project badge sits close to the following title, weakening row boundaries.

strength: The open menu pairs legible workspace names with distinctive icons and checks Planner. Inbox is named prominently after arrival.
concern: The closed three-line button gives no workspace name and the Today title gives no clue that Planner is active.

strength: All five controls fit on one line at 440 pt. At 390 pt the two dates stay together on a new left-aligned line, and the schedule remains visible beside the circle above.
concern: Notes starts under the time gutter, far left of the task title. The change of alignment interrupts the path from the title into its notes.

strength: Space after the project badges clearly separates even consecutive tagged rows. Notes and both control groups in the expanded card share the title alignment.
concern: The roomy spacing reduces the visible list: the 1 PM task reaches the bottom toolbar and its project badge is partly obscured.

strength: Inbox is visible beside the checked Planner segment before switching. The check moves to Inbox under its matching title.
concern: The persistent strip uses a full row above the list, and the isolated dash in the Inbox footer has no clear meaning.

strength: Aligned times, circles and flags make even the two-line print-proof row traceable across the screen.
concern: The Studio badge nearly meets the following title in the collapsed list. The expanded card also puts the time and date chips very close to its edges.

strength: A divider gathers properties across the card width. The schedule and deadline lead the group at both widths, with all values visible.
concern: At 390 pt the project and two icons restart at the far right on a second line, leaving a diagonal gap in the reading order.

strength: The gap after each project badge separates it from the next title. The expanded title, notes and controls have distinct vertical intervals.
concern: The expanded card leaves a broad empty column below the time while stacking the controls on the right. The project labels are small at list scale.

strength: The Planner label and chevron identify the switcher. Inbox appears by name in the opened strip and in both the title and switcher on arrival.
concern: Opening the strip replaces the date and plus controls and changes the meaning of the entire bottom row.

strength: The menu appears under the title with a check beside Planner, leaving the date navigator and plus in the footer.
concern: Today with a downward chevron can read as a date selector. Planner is named only once the menu opens.

strength: The Studio badge stays close to its own wrapped title with a visible gap before the next task. The expanded card keeps notes and the two control groups distinct.
concern: The small gray project names take more attention to read than the times or trailing deadlines.

strength: The open menu presents three labeled destinations with different icons and a clear check on Planner.
concern: The closed three-line button gives no workspace name, and Today above the list gives little clue that Planner is active.

strength: The full-width property area fits a single line at 440 pt. At 390 pt the dates wrap together, and both lines share the same left edge.
concern: The Notes placeholder begins under the time instead of the title, making the title-to-notes transition less direct.

strength: Notes, project controls and date controls share the title edge. Property order and grouping are identical at both widths.
concern: At 440 pt the preserved leading time gutter leaves enough space unused that the card still needs two lines of controls.

strength: A complete Choose the frame finish row fits above the toolbar, while the time and completion circle still lead directly to the expanded title.
concern: The small Studio chips have little separation from the following titles, especially above Order replacement hinges.

strength: The named Planner button and chevron disclose the switcher. Its checked Planner choice, Inbox destination and persistent date and plus controls are individually identifiable.
concern: The open choices bar cuts across late-afternoon task text and repeats Planner immediately above the Planner button.

strength: 10:00 AM stays aligned with its completion circle. All five controls fit on one line at 440 pt and the two dates stay together at 390 pt.
concern: Notes shares the title inset while Studio restarts at the far left, giving successive lines in the same card different reading origins.

strength: Inbox sits in the same visible segment before and after arrival, and the check moves from Planner to Inbox. The bottom date arrows and plus occupy separate positions.
concern: The permanent selector occupies a full line above the list. In Inbox, a lone dash still occupies the former date position.

strength: The left-aligned Notes and Studio chip establish a shared edge below the timed title. The paired dates remain readable on one line at either width.
concern: At 390 pt the control group needs a second line, leaving empty space to the right of the three short chips.

strength: The Planner chevron leads to a clearly checked Planner segment and a named Inbox segment. The destination then appears on both the page and the switcher.
concern: Opening choices replaces the date and capture controls entirely, so the bottom row changes meaning between the first two views.

strength: The Studio tag beneath the two-line print-proof task has visible space before the floor-plan title. The expanded card gives Notes and both chip rows their own lines.
concern: The looser spacing leaves only a sliver of Choose the frame finish above the date toolbar, and the gray project labels remain small.

strength: The compact rhythm exposes Call the courier and part of the following task while retaining the fixed time and flag columns.
concern: The expanded title sits close to the card top and its date chips close to the bottom. The next dimmed title begins immediately below, crowding the card boundary.

strength: The labeled Planner chevron opens a checked workspace strip directly above it. The date arrows and capture plus remain visible in place.
concern: The open strip covers part of the afternoon list and repeats the Planner label on two adjacent levels.

strength: Space below Studio separates the wrapped proof task from the floor-plan row. The expanded card preserves the time, circle and title alignment.
concern: The 10:00 AM label nearly touches the expanded card edge even as Notes and the two property rows have generous space around them. Project tags are small.

strength: The completion circles mark the center of each row, including the wrapped titles. The frame-finish row and its tag fit fully above the toolbar.
concern: The small gray project pills require a closer look than the titles, particularly in the group from cover artwork through accessibility findings.

strength: Planner and Inbox appear together above the list. The check and white segment move to Inbox on arrival, while the date and capture controls occupy a separate bottom bar.
concern: The persistent strip costs about one short row of list space, and Inbox repeats as both the heading and the selected segment.

strength: At 440 points all five controls form one line. At 390 both dates move together to a second line and retain their full labels.
concern: Notes moves from the title column to the left card inset, directly beneath the schedule. The time also sits very close to the card edge.

strength: The fixed time and completion columns make it easy to find the 10 AM task in both states. The compact list shows tasks down to the afternoon.
concern: The short gap between a project pill and the next title competes with the gap inside a row. The adjacent floor-plan title also crowds the expanded card shadow.

strength: Notes shares the title inset, while the controls start at the card inset. That fits all five at 440 points and keeps both dates together at 390.
concern: The leading 10:00 AM comes close to the rounded card edge at both widths, especially compared with the more generous inset of the property buttons.

strength: A labeled workspace chevron and a checked three-way selector use the same bottom edge. The choices occupy a single band clear of the list.
concern: While the choices are open the date arrows and capture plus disappear, so their usual positions temporarily serve workspace navigation.

strength: The circle, title and trailing flag stay aligned even where a title wraps. In the expanded card, Notes and both groups of pills share the title edge.
concern: The extra space between Notes and the pills helps distinguish them, but the taller card pushes the next task down and leaves little space outside its top edge.

strength: The Planner button names the workspace and its chevron signals more choices. The raised chooser marks Planner while the date and plus keep their positions.
concern: The chooser repeats Planner directly above the Planner button and covers the bottom task rows.

strength: The 10:00 AM label stays immediately left of the circle. Full-width properties fit on one line at 440 pt and both dates stay together at 390 pt.
concern: Notes starts beneath the time column, far to the left of the title it describes. The time label sits very close to the card edge.

strength: Notes lines up with the wrapped title. The separate property row uses the full width at 440 pt and keeps both date pills together on a second line at 390 pt.
concern: The 10:00 AM text starts almost flush with the left card edge at both widths, tighter than the inset around the properties.

strength: The completion circles separate rows as titles change height, and the expanded card fits two distinct groups of pills with visible padding underneath.
concern: The small gray project badges recede to the point that Studio and Renovation require a closer read than the adjacent time and deadline labels.

strength: The chooser occupies the same bottom strip as the Planner control, with three named destinations and a check beside Planner. Inbox is named on arrival.
concern: Opening the choices removes the date and capture controls from view. The isolated dash in the Inbox date position has no visible explanation.

strength: The consistent title and flag columns keep deadlines easy to pick out while the dense list shows tasks all the way through Call the courier.
concern: Project badges sit close to the next title, especially Studio above Reply to Mina. The expanded card's final date pills also run close to its bottom edge.

strength: Inbox is visible beside the checked Planner before switching. The check and selected segment move together on arrival, well apart from date browsing and capture.
concern: Reserving a full strip below Today pushes the first task down. On arrival, Inbox appears in both the page title and the selected segment.
